key_insight: This paper shows how to turn standard neural networks into discretization-agnostic neural operators that can learn directly from continuous scientific data. The result is models that generalize more reliably across different grid resolutions and simulation settings.
problem_solved: Many AI models for scientific computing depend on a fixed discretization, so they struggle when data resolution changes. This work addresses the challenge of building architectures that operate on function spaces rather than a single sampled representation.
method: Extend popular neural architectures into neural operators that map between function spaces instead of fixed-size arrays.
Design the models to be discretization-agnostic, so the same learned operator can work across multiple resolutions.
Use continuous scientific data as the training signal to improve resolution-independent generalization.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this makes it easier to deploy models for scientific simulation, PDE learning, and surrogate modeling without retraining for every mesh or grid. It improves robustness and portability across numerical settings.

paper_title: Principled approaches for extending neural architectures to function spaces for operator learning
paper_authors: Julius Berner, Miguel Liu-Schiaffini, Jean Kossaifi, Valentin Duruisseaux, Boris Bonev
